native#1 lineage unreadable — no chrome, controls, or density evidence in the composite
native#10 no genuine window/traffic-lights/toolbar anywhere in image
#6/#8/#11/#12/#13/#14 and native#3/#4/#5/#7/#9 n/a — static marketing card has no paragraphs, forms, actions, selection, sidebar, toolbar, or focus states

tokens.notes: near-black navy marketing backdrop with radial blue glow; NOT a window background
brand blue, more saturated/indigo than macOS system blue #0088FF/#0091FF; carries every non-white element

tokens.value: white #F5F4F7, bold geometric-humanist sans (SF Pro Display Bold-class)

tokens.notes: blue is accent, gray is genuine de-emphasis

patterns.key_values: indicative time card: dark translucent rounded tile, ~16px pad, 3 left-aligned rows (flag+city / big time / accent-blue abbr + optional gray day chip); marketing-rendered, unconfirmed as shipped UI

signature_moves: World-network marketing trope: 3D dotted globe + great-circle connection arcs + floating city time-cards + a physical 3D clock — competent but category-generic, not a distinctive design signature
One-accent discipline: a single electric blue is the only chromatic event against near-black; Von Restorff by construction
Jakob's-Law card schema: time cards borrow Apple's world-clock/Notification-tile anatomy verbatim (flag + city + big time + abbr) so the concept parses in under a second
defects: Accent-binding risk (unconfirmed) — brand blue ~#1666FF is more saturated than macOS system accent; if carried into app selection/focus/primary-action chrome it would violate the accent-is-the-user's-accent rule. Cannot confirm without an app screenshot
No verifiable UI evidence — cover shows no window; real spacing grid, control density, chrome, and native-tells are entirely unaudited (staged 9:41 placeholder + glow)
Marketing-render contrast watch — brand-blue abbreviations on dark navy card sit near the 4.5:1 text floor; hairline card border likely under the 3:1 non-text floor (render-only)

aesthetic.direction: Neo-grotesque product (dark) — near-black navy ramp + one electric-blue accent + glass-ish translucent tiles + glow; the model-reflex dark-utility marketing look (frontend-aesthetic-direction warns this is a default, not a distinctive choice)
peers: macOS World Clock / Notification Center tiles (card grammar)
aesthetic.cluster_hint: electric-dark-utility (brand-only; do not open a UI cluster from marketing evidence)

psychology: Von Restorff / signal-detection — single electric-blue accent against near-black makes every blue element (tagline, feature glyphs, card abbr, links) pre-attentively pop
Jakob's Law — time cards mimic Apple's trained world-clock/widget schema (flag + city + time + abbr), so the concept is instantly legible
Aesthetic-usability effect / 50ms first impression — polished 3D render + glow buys a quality halo, but sells perceived quality on a marketing surface rather than proving app usability
Miller/Cowan chunking — exactly 4 feature chunks, within the 3-5 comfortable band
notes: CRITICAL: cover.png is a marketing composite with NO captured app window (no traffic lights, toolbar, sidebar, menu bar, or frame). The timezone cards are rendered marketing floats (9:41 Apple placeholder, Apple flag emoji), read as indicative card grammar only, NOT a screenshot of the running app. Contributes brand evidence + one indicative widget-card pattern and ZERO native macOS canon evidence. Lineage/era unknowable from this image; Apple-ecosystem INTENT is clear (Built-for-macOS badge, SF-like type, Notification-tile styling) but native vs Catalyst vs SwiftUI vs Electron cannot be told. Do NOT cluster this app or promote any token to canon. Rubric/native scores apply to the indicative card component only and are heavily caveated. Icon.png (1024) is out of scope for this UI digest (Workflow A only) — a separate icon digest should handle it. A real app-window screenshot is needed before any native evidence can be taken.
